newsitem.title: USA: Santa Fe Pacific Gold closes out gold put options.
newsitem.headline: Santa Fe Pacific Gold closes out gold put options.

text.p: Santa Fe Pacific Gold Corp said Friday it had closed out for cash its remaining purchased put options representing 900,000 ounces of gold and its written call options on 300,000 ounces of gold.
Santa Fe received $17 million from the transaction, chairman Patrick James said.
In addition, between January and March, 300,000 ounces worth of put options were exercised with $6.7 million cash received and 100,000 ounces worth of calls expired unexercised.

The net gain of $23.7 million relating to the total 1.2 million ounces of put options and 400,000 ounces of calls was recorded as deferred revenue which will be recognized in gold sales revenue during applicable future production periods.
"Current market prices have provided cash value on the put options, which had strike prices of $375 per ounce," chairman James said.
The options were purchased in 1995 but this in-the-money condition did not occur until recently, he said.
"Since the company has been able to maintain its deferred forward sales contract position at target levels, the decision was made to close out the options for cash prior to their expiration."
Santa Fe Pacific Gold is one of the largest gold mining companies in North America with mines in California and Nevada.
